lines.text: Friday the 13th has come round again.
lines.say: Friday the thirteenth has come round again.

lines.text: For the third time this year, which is as many as a year can hold.
So why is it unlucky? Nobody really knows.
13 at one table was already thought to be bad luck.
lines.say: Thirteen at one table was already thought to be bad luck.

lines.text: In the 1880s, a New York club set out to mock it. 13 men dined together, in room 13.
lines.say: In the eighteen eighties, a New York club set out to mock it. Thirteen men dined together, in room thirteen.

lines.text: Then, in 1907, came a novel called Friday, the Thirteenth, about a broker who crashes the stock market on that very day.
lines.say: Then, in nineteen oh seven, came a novel called Friday, the Thirteenth, about a broker who crashes the stock market on that very day.

lines.text: The book sold. The fear stuck.
In Italy, the unlucky day is Friday the 17th. In Spain, it is Tuesday the 13th.
lines.say: In Italy, the unlucky day is Friday the seventeenth. In Spain, it is Tuesday the thirteenth.

lines.text: The next one is in August. You have nine months to prepare.
